item.title: Some issues with dose administration aids/monitored dosage systems
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody Monitored dosage systems (or dose administration aids) are widely used but it is important to reduce their inappropriate use by ensuring they are only issued on a case-by-case basis to address specific practical problems of medicines adherence. item.title: Ifosfamide-induced encephalopathy and concomitant use of netupitant/palonosetron in a patient with soft tissue sarcoma: a case report
item.description: Agreement I do not AgreeBody A number of case reports have linked the administration of aprepitant with an increased risk of ifosfamide-induced encephalopathy (IIE), and it has even been discussed as a potential trigger. The reason given is elevated ifosfamide levels or those of neurotoxic metabolites. Is this plausible? Ifosfamide itself is pharmacodynamically inactive.
